title: Do wildfires that start in smaller barrier compartments end smaller? A re-executed pre-registered confirmatory test in northeast Washington
abstract: Trees Cannot Cut holds that wildfires end where closed loops of holdable features stop them. A consequence is that a fire which starts inside a smaller compartment of mapped barriers should end smaller. After a pilot in the Okanogan, Methow and Chelan region of Washington, a confirmatory replication (P1C v1.4) was pre-registered for the adjoining northeast Washington region. Its plan, code, blind predictor table and critical values were hash-frozen and timestamped before any fire size was requested, and the plan went through five independent audits. The single confirmatory test regresses log10 final fire size (FPA FOD, 1992-2024) on log10 compartment area under definition B (TIGER roads, NHD water and LANDFIRE non-burnable fuel), controlling for gridMET fire-danger percentile, fuel group, cause, month, year, barrier density, road distance and 40 km regional fixed effects (model M2R). It is decided on the interval beta +/- 2.53 x max(two-way, year-clustered SE). We re-ran the frozen registered script, unchanged, on the registered input files, whose SHA-256 hashes all match the registration. The re-run gives the published numbers: on 11,314 ignitions, beta = 0.0531 (registered interval 0.0228 to 0.0835, T = 4.42), so the decision is SUPPORTED and the pre-specified reading is REPLICATED. A tenfold larger compartment goes with final fires about 13% larger. The result has clear limits, all from the study's own pre-specified checks. The study is observational and does not show that barriers stop fires, nor how much of the association runs through suppression access. Without the 40 km regional terms (S13, the pilot's model M2) the estimate is 0.033 and does not pass its critical value of 3.93. Lightning-caused fires show no effect (S6a: -0.015, 95% CI -0.062 to 0.033); the association is in human-caused fires. Counting burn scars from the previous ten years as barriers shrinks the estimate to 0.020 (S5).

claims.text: Running the frozen registered P1C v1.4 script (code/run_test.py, unchanged, via code/rerun_p1c.py) on the registered input files gives, for the registered primary test (H2, definition B, model M2R): n = 11,314 ignitions, beta = 0.0531 (0.05313557) log10 final fire size per log10 compartment area, max(two-way, year-clustered) SE = 0.0120, registered interval beta +/- 2.53 x max SE = [0.0228, 0.0835], decision SUPPORTED under the frozen rule (SUPPORTED iff beta - C2 x max SE > 0), and pre-specified reading REPLICATED. The script's input check against the registered FREEZE.json passed (inputs_verified true). This is the output of the frozen registered analysis on the registered inputs; it is an observational association and does not show that barriers stop fires.

next_steps: If the verifier labels C1 TESTED, P4 can move to the next registered real-fire test (e.g. the Okanogan-Methow-Chelan pilot, if its frozen script and inputs are published at a pinned commit). Note for the verifier image and future runs: the frozen run_test.py imports scipy.stats (t critical value), so scipy is required in addition to numpy and pandas. The results/p1c_primary.json hash obtained here (numpy 2.5.4, pandas 3.1.1, scipy 1.18.1) differs from the 2026-11-09 hash in INPUTS.json (numpy 2.5.3, pandas 3.0.5); all reported numbers agree with P1C_RESULTS.md to the published precision. No new analysis was added, by design.
